text: In June 2026, the applicant applied to the Committee of Adjustment for variances to the City-wide Zoning By-law 569-2013 in order to allow the construction of a six-storey apartment building, containing 54 dwelling units (the “Application”). The applicant sought eleven variances relating to the maximum permitted building length, minimum front, rear and side yard setbacks, minimum landscaping area, minimum drive aisle width, parking space dimensions, visitor parking requirements, loading space requirements, and minimum bicycle parking access aisle width. In its report dated July 6, 2026, City Planning Staff recommended that the Committee of Adjustment defer the Application. City Planning Staff sought further discussions with the applicant to improve the proposed built form and requested that the Committee of Adjustment defer this Application until the next scheduled meeting (the Staff…

City Council on July 29 and 30, 2026, adopted the following: 1. City Council direct the City Solicitor to seek party status at the Toronto Local Appeal Body, and to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body hearing, with appropriate City staff, in order to support the Committee of Adjustment’s decision to refuse Application A0208/26NY, respecting 340 St Clements Avenue. 2. City Council authorize the City Solicitor to retain outside consultants as necessary. 3. City Council authorize the City Solicitor to negotiate a resolution regarding 340 St Clements Avenue (Application A0208/26NY) and authorize the City Solicitor to resolve the matter on behalf of the City, at their discretion, after consultation with the Ward Councillor and the Director of Community Planning, North York District.
